model.title: A country has 30 million people and 600,000 km². Density?

blocks.title: Sort into: Physical factor / Human factor
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Physical factor, Human factor.
blocks.answer: Physical factor: fertile soil; reliable rainfall; flat land. Human factor: jobs in cities; ports and trade; roads and railways

keywords.def: how people are spread out over an area
the number of people per square kilometre

questions.q: Country X: 10 million people, 100,000 km². Density?
Why is the Sahara sparsely populated?
questions.a: Very little water and extreme heat

questions.q: Give one human factor that attracts people.
Core: Using the density map, describe the pattern of population in Africa (PQE) in the portal response box, then calculate densities for three countries from the data table.
questions.a: A PQE description with named places, and three correct densities

questions.q: Extend: Explain why Egypt's population is concentrated along the Nile.
questions.a: Water and fertile soil in a desert country; farming, cities and transport along the river

questions.q: Stretch: Why can density figures hide differences within a country?
questions.a: An average hides crowded cities and empty deserts
A) People per square kilometre. Density divides people by area, so we can compare countries of different sizes.

questions.q: Big question: why do Egyptians live on so little land?
questions.a: The Nile gives water and fertile soil in a desert; the rest is too dry
